children: AMD rallied on AI demand, hitting intraday and close records near $615–$625, briefly topping $1 trillion market cap. Stock jumped ~9–10% in its biggest session and gained ~173–180% YTD.
AMD raised its 2030 server CPU addressable market to over $120B and sees a broader data-center CPU opportunity near $220B, citing agentic AI demand and potential 1:1 CPU-to-GPU server ratios
AMD expands AI portfolio beyond CPUs/GPUs to include accelerators, networking and rack-level systems for hyperscalers, targeting end-to-end datacenter needs for large-scale AI workloads.
AMD: CEO Lisa Su says agentic CPU demand adds to GPU use and that 'agentic sandboxes' are the main driver of rising server CPU demand, linking agentic workloads to higher CPU needs.
AMD raised prices ~10% on select high-performance computing chips, citing higher manufacturing costs and strong demand to boost operating margins and EBITDA.
AMD jumped Monday, topping Nvidia as traders cited rising AI inference and server-CPU demand, driven by hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending and interest in AI apps like Meta’s Muse.
AMD pairs EPYC server CPUs with Instinct accelerators and open software, plus AMD Inference Microservices, to run diverse server and inference workloads across hardware platforms.
